subject: explorable-load
note: the patched client against this world, two portal crossings in 28 s: into 146 Lakeside County with is_explorable 1, which cost 4984 client ticks (7.0 s) from its spawn request to its players request, and back into 148 Ascalon City, which cost 640 (0.90 s). The world tick stream is silent for 562 ticks after the spawn point and then arrives in one batch of six: the client is inside its loading screen. Server side of the same two travels: 5138 ms and 849 ms (logs/world-8001.log, not committed). See docs/23-initialization-protocol.md, The explorable.

subject: login-to-spawn
note: the retail client against the retail server, unfiltered, both directions: character select, a character switch, entering the world, then the inventory, guild and party windows. 1967 records (1958 StoC, 9 CToS), 112 distinct StoC headers. The first capture made after the sniffer array-size and event-ring fixes: the largest drain is 579 records, and 0x008A and 0x00B5 are 264 bytes each. 0x00B5 carries a count of 50 and the 50-byte blob Rurik recorded (research/Rurik/studies/newopcodes/FINDINGS.md). No CToS 0x45: no setting was changed. StoC copies stop at 512 bytes, so 0x00DB (520) and 0x0197 (1032) are clipped. Sanitised after capture: 138 records of 15 text-carrying headers have no payload (the file header lists them).

subject: preferences
note: the retail client in an outpost, unfiltered, both directions, 18 s: the four weapon sets unticked and ticked again. 865 records, two of them from the client, both 0x45 (the character preferences upload): seq 476 and 696, a count of 50 and 50 bytes that differ only at offset 15 (00 unticked, 3c ticked). Only world updates follow each upload: the server answers nothing. Sanitised after capture: 7 records of text-carrying headers have no payload (the file header lists the headers).

subject: preferences
note: the retail client, unfiltered, both directions, 22 s: two weapon sets unticked, then a map travel. 3650 records. The upload is seq 466 (0x45, a count of 50, 24 at offset 15); the next load returns the same 50 bytes in 0x00B5 at seq 1608, between 0x008A at 1607 and 0x00DB at 1609. Sanitised after capture: 241 records of text-carrying headers have no payload, and three short letter runs left in the client buffer are zeroed (seq 2137, 2537, 2962).

subject: character_creation-armor-color
note: the retail client, unfiltered, both directions, 68 s: a whole character creation. Profession changes at seq 658, 1099, 1156, 1186 and 1241, each 0x60 followed by seven 0x84; four armour colours changed by hand at seq 1272, 1276, 1280 and 1284 (slots 2, 6, 3, 5, colour 5), each answered with 0x0161, 0x015A, 0x015B; the confirm at seq 1296 with every create option ticked, answered with 0x0099 and 0x0188; then the new character's first load (0x91, 0x88, 0x90 at seq 1303-1972), which opens a cinematic, the cinematic skipped (0x63 at seq 5429), and the character standing where a new character starts. Cleaned after capture: names, the client's computer info and the players-request identifier are removed.
